- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to underpredict upward moves; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ 0.33), model often overpredicts downward moves; adjust downward by 1–2% to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model consistently underestimates price spikes in the 3rd–5th day of a new trend (especially after sentiment shift); add 0.5–1.5% buffer to forecast for early trend acceleration.
- Model overestimates mean reversion in 30-day horizon; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% if sentiment is neutral or slightly positive.
- If sentiment shows strong momentum (e.g., 3+ consecutive high sentiment values), model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead with slight upward bias.
- When true outcome exceeds model by >3% in 30d, check if sentiment was positive 3–5 days prior — if yes, increase next forecast by 1–2% to capture momentum.
- If model forecast is consistently below true outcome by >2% over 3–5 days, sentiment is likely bullish — increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for next period.
